thread:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — ran a long-run profile on shard-12 and noticed tenant `tdx` KV residency steadily climbing with longctx > 32k. Paging rate spikes and slab fragmentation increases after ~90m. putting raw numbers here: P99_residency: 72k pages, paging_rate: 480/s :astonished:
Sam Huang: Ugh. Any quick artifact? flame graph or top stacks? :eyes:
Maya Patel: pasted a small flame snippet from perf-top:
```
kv_pagewalk         42.3%
slab_alloc          18.1%
kv_eviction_worker  12.4%
page_compactor       9.6%
memcopy_async        7.2%
idle                 10.4%
```
Maya Patel: Observations: frequent small allocations cause slab fragmentation; eviction worker gets starved which lets residency grow. Notably memcopy_async time goes up in same window — might be contention with batching/kernel scheduling.
Kevin O'Leary: Sounds like a noisy-tenant pattern where repeated longctx append + small frees cause reuse failure. We should enforce a per-tenant residency soft-cap + a reclaim kick instead of only global eviction.
Devon Ramos: Also worth checking if batching heuristics cause more frequent KV writes that bork free lists. Large dynamic batches + small token outputs = allocator churn. Could be a heuristic mismatch.
Sam Huang: I'll try two quick experiments on a canary: 1) reduce max_residency_fraction for tenant tdx from 0.6->0.45, 2) bump eviction worker concurrency from 2->4. Both low-risk.
infra-bot: ALERT shard-12 paging-rate spike at 2026-03-14T18:12:05Z — paging_rate 502/s, host load 4.2 — automated throttles not hit.
Maya Patel: For mitigation we can also try changing reclaim policy to "aggressive_reclaim" for tdx temporarily. config snippet:
```
{
  "tenant": "tdx",
  "kv": {
    "max_residency_fraction": 0.45,
    "reclaim_policy": "aggressive_reclaim",
    "eviction_concurrency": 4
  }
}
```
Kevin O'Leary: We should also add a unit perf test that simulates longctx append patterns + small chunky prompt generation to reproduce slab fragmentation in CI. I can own that.
Sam Huang: I'll run a perf regression after the canary change. If eviction worker change lowers p99_residency by >20% we can roll to prod.
Devon Ramos: One more thing — check kernel selection telemetry around the memcopy path. If we fall back to a slower memcpy kernel under certain batch shapes, it could lengthen eviction cycles. I'll grep the kernel-selector logs.
Maya Patel: Great. Action items: Sam run canary + perf run (today), Kevin add reproduction unit test, Devon inspect kernel-selection logs and memcopy fallback, I'll prepare rollback playbook for quick revert.
Sam Huang: Running canary now. Will post results in ~30m. :thumbsup:
Maya Patel: thanks — if we need an emergency quota we can set tenant to "limited" via `rictl tenant set-quota tdx --kv-pages 50000`
infra-bot: noted — no auto-enforcement triggered.
Sam Huang: Canary finished: paging_rate dropped to 210/s, p99_residency down ~34%, but we see a small latency tail for 90s during compaction. Logs: `compaction: pause_ms=92`
Maya Patel: good trade for now. I'll schedule follow-up to tune compaction window and reclamation thresholds.
Kevin O'Leary: Filed PR for the CI repro test: #4381.
Devon Ramos: kernel-selector log shows a fallback to host-memcopy-cpu-path when batch shape is [1,>4k] — that aligns with the memcopy_async increase. I'll open an issue to prioritize a faster memcpy kernel for that shape.
Maya Patel: Nice. We'll document the temporary tenant soft-cap + kernel work in the runbook. Thanks all. :pray:
